description: Single-panel stacked bar chart reporting the contribution of each strengthening mechanism to the yield strength of Fe-6.8Al low-density steel. Y-axis: "Strength contribution (MPa)", 0-2400 with major ticks every 200 MPa. X-axis carries three condition labels printed exactly as "98%CR", "750°C, 5min", "750°C, 60min". Every bar is stacked in the same order, bottom to top: red = Lattice frictional stress, black = Solid solution, blue = Grain boundary, magenta = Dislocations, green = Ordering, matching the two-column legend. Printed above the bars are the totals "YS = 1800MPa" (98%CR), "YS = 700MPa" (750°C, 5min) and "YS = 265MPa" (750°C, 60min); dashed horizontal lines mark these levels and each bar carries a small error bar at its top. In the 98%CR bar, grain boundary (blue, roughly 200-900 MPa) and dislocations (magenta, roughly 900-1750 MPa) dominate, whereas solid solution (black) is small and ordering (green) is only a thin cap. Annealing progressively shrinks every contribution, so after 60 min only grain boundary (~200 MPa) and solid solution remain appreciable. The figure demonstrates that the drop in yield strength from 1800 to 265 MPa with longer annealing is governed mainly by loss of dislocation and grain-boundary strengthening; the caption labels the three bars (a)-(c), though no panel letters appear in the image.

subfigures.description: Stacked bar for condition '98%CR' with total labelled 'YS = 1800MPa'. Bottom red (Lattice frictional stress) is a small sliver, black (Solid solution) reaches about the 200 MPa gridline, blue (Grain boundary) is the largest segment spanning roughly 200-900 MPa, magenta (Dislocations) spans roughly 900-1750 MPa, and a thin green (Ordering) cap closes the bar at 1800 MPa. A small error bar sits at the bar top.

Stacked bar for '750°C, 5min' with total labelled 'YS = 700MPa'. Red bottom sliver, black up to roughly 120 MPa, blue (Grain boundary) up to roughly 500 MPa, a thinner magenta (Dislocations) band to about 650 MPa and a green (Ordering) cap to 700 MPa; error bar at the top.

Stacked bar for '750°C, 60min' with total labelled 'YS = 265MPa'. All contributions are strongly reduced: red sliver at the base, black to roughly 80 MPa, blue (Grain boundary) to about 200 MPa, thin magenta band and a green (Ordering) cap completing 265 MPa; error bar at the top.

observations.observation: The figure is a single stacked bar chart with y-axis labelled 'Strength contribution (MPa)', scaled 0-2400 in 200 MPa major increments.
Three bars are labelled on the x-axis exactly as '98%CR', '750°C, 5min' and '750°C, 60min'.
The legend lists five mechanisms with colours: Ordering (green), Grain boundary (blue), Solid solution (black), Dislocations (magenta) and Lattice frictional stress (red).
Total yield strength is printed above each bar as 'YS = 1800MPa', 'YS = 700MPa' and 'YS = 265MPa' for 98%CR, 750°C/5min and 750°C/60min respectively.
Dashed horizontal lines run across the plot at the three yield-strength levels (1800, 700 and 265 MPa), marking the top of each bar.
Each bar is stacked in the identical bottom-to-top order red (Lattice frictional stress), black (Solid solution), blue (Grain boundary), magenta (Dislocations), green (Ordering).

In the 98%CR bar the blue Grain boundary segment is the largest contribution (from about the 200 MPa gridline to about 900 MPa) and the magenta Dislocations segment is the second largest (about 900 to about 1750 MPa).
Small error bars are drawn at the top of all three stacked bars; their magnitude is not numerically labelled.
The red Lattice frictional stress segment is a small basal sliver in all three bars, well below the 200 MPa gridline.
The black Solid solution segment shrinks from roughly the 200 MPa gridline in 98%CR to below about 120 MPa after 5 min and below about 80 MPa after 60 min annealing.
Total yield strength decreases monotonically with annealing: 1800 MPa (98%CR) > 700 MPa (750°C, 5 min) > 265 MPa (750°C, 60 min), while the green Ordering cap remains a thin top layer in all bars.

The caption states the figure is a bar graph showing the contribution of various strengthening mechanisms to the yield strength of Fe-6.8Al low-density steel after 98% cold rolling and isothermal annealing at 750 °C for 5 min and 60 min.
The caption labels the three bars as (a) 98% cold rolling, (b) 750 °C 5 min and (c) 750 °C 60 min, but no (a)/(b)/(c) letters are visible in the image itself.

The citing text states the strengthening contributions considered are (i) solid solution, (ii) presence of ordered phase and (iii) at least one further mechanism (sentence truncated in the supplied excerpt).
